### Do Not Touch the Lord’s Anointed
Author: Augustus Lopes
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/do-not-touch-the-lords-anointed
Passage: 1 Samuel 24:6
Points:
- David spared Saul because he recognized that Saul held a God-ordained royal office.
- This text is often improperly used today to shield church leaders from accountability or criticism.
- David’s respect for the office did not prevent him from directly confronting Saul’s unjust behavior.
- Rather than taking personal revenge, David submitted the matter to the righteous judgment of God.
- True Christian leaders do not silence concerns with slogans, but lead with truth, humility, and integrity.

### A Clear Conscience
Author: Pastor Chuck Swindoll
Site: Insight for Living Ministries
URL: https://insight.org/resources/daily-devotional/individual/a-clear-conscience
Passage: 1 Samuel 24:12
Points:
- David demonstrated personal integrity by confronting Saul directly rather than talking behind his back.
- When Saul was vulnerable, David chose restraint and placed ultimate justice in the hands of the Lord.
- Responding with righteousness does not guarantee that an enemy will permanently turn and change.
- Believers are called to speak truth in love and keep a clear conscience regardless of the outcome.

### Day 32: 1 Samuel 24:1–22
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-32-1-samuel-24-122.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 24:11
Points:
- David’s remorse over cutting Saul’s robe showed a conscience sharply attuned to the Holy Spirit.
- Genuine conviction in David’s heart produced an immediate stop to harmful behavior.
- David exercised supernatural self-restraint when handed an easy opportunity to take vengeance.
- He withdrew from harming his persecutor because reverence for God outweighed his desire for payback.
- Yielding to the Spirit when tempted to retaliate protects believers from costly, destructive errors.
